newsitem.title: IRAQ: Over 2.5 mln Iraqi families without power - minister.
newsitem.headline: Over 2.5 mln Iraqi families without power - minister.

text.p: An Iraqi minister said on Monday over 2.5 million families in Iraq were without electricity and blasted the United States for blocking contracts on power spare parts under the country's oil deal with the United Nations.

Industry and Minerals Minister Adnan Abdul-Majeed said the United States had allowed only three contracts out of 32 presented to the U.N. to go through. "The U.S. put the rest on hold for unjustified reasons," he said.
"Power does not reach more than 2.5 million families. And it is summer. Imagine the hardships," he said at a news conference.
He said power cuts were affecting performance of hospitals, industry and agriculture. Housewives complained that unsteady current and frequent cuts put many of their household utensils out of order.

Abdul-Majeed blamed Washington for the blackouts which he expected to increase during the summer season, and he urged U.N. security council members to put pressure on the U.S. to let the contracts go through.
"The memorandum of understanding (oil deal) exposed the falsity of the American administration and its defence of human rights," he said.
Iraq's oil deal with U.N., which went into effect last December, is worth $2 billion in six months. The first six months end on June 9.
He said power allocations under the deal amounted to $36 million but only three contracts had been approved so far all worth $387,515. "Not a single spare has reached Iraq yet," he said.
Iraq's power plants were a target of air and missile attacks during the 1991 Gulf War which forced Iraqi troops out of Kuwait.
Abdul-Majeed said certain plants had been turned into heaps of rubble but his engineers had been able to bring them back to life.
Iraq had suffered no blackouts in the first three years after the war but the cuts had increased recently due to what Abdul-Majeed said were "severe shortages of spare parts."

"Only days separate us from the end of the six month period and no spare part has reached us...Under the deal the approval of the contract and the provision of spare parts should take place in the same period," he said.
He was determined to get the spare parts which were urgently needed to repair four major power plants in the country.
"On our part we are committed to the memorandum of understanding," he said.
